items.quote: Where that True Physick is to be Found
items.note: The chapter is headed as the place where the True Physick is to be found.

items.quote: thing that God created Good is extreamly perfect and incorruptible, as the heaven
items.note: What God created good is perfect and incorruptible; the heaven is the example.

items.quote: whatsoever is in these sublunary inferiour things hath a twofold Nature
items.note: Things below the moon are said to have two natures.

items.quote: a perfect and an imperfect, that is, a fift Essence and the dreggs may be separated one from the other by fire
items.note: The twofold nature is glossed: the perfect is a fift Essence, the imperfect the dreggs; fire can part them.

items.quote: the true medicine (or Physick) is wrapt up in rindes, barks, matrixes, receptacles, husks, garment and cottages
items.note: The true medicine is said to be wrapped up in coverings.

items.quote: as Almonds and all kernells are covered with bark and rind
items.note: The covering of the medicine is put as a likeness: kernel inside bark and rind.

items.quote: the same must be seperated from the impure Elements by the artificiall Anotomy of Chymists before we can come at the pure Medicine
items.note: The medicine is to be separated from the impure Elements by the Chymists' Anotomy before the pure Medicine is reached.

items.quote: the bonds are loosed by art and industry, and the faculties of healing set at liberty
items.note: Art and industry loose the bonds and free the healing faculties.

items.quote: Wheat doth norgrow without a place, nor can we have meale without bran, neither is hony without a sting.
items.note: Margin note gives three likenesses of a good thing joined with something else (meal with bran, honey with sting).

items.quote: Such Secrets are regenerated without any complexion of qualities.
items.note: Margin note: such Secrets are regenerated without complexion of qualities.

items.quote: those three Families of Nature, the Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
items.what: three Families of Nature, the Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
items.note: Nature is set out as three Families.

items.quote: there is contained that True and specifix Physick of materiall distempers
items.note: The True and specifix Physick of material distempers is contained in the three Families.

items.quote: which as hath been said, doth not consist in the four outward
items.note: Points back to an earlier place where this was said.

items.quote: doth not consist in the four outward, naked, superficiary and Relollaceous qualities (as Theophrastus learnedly discourseth)
items.name: Theophrastus
items.note: The denial that the Physick lies in the four outward qualities is given with Theophrastus named as discoursing of it.

items.quote: it is a certaine specifix vertue concealed in the very Seeds, naturally proceeding without art
items.note: The Physick is said to be a specifix vertue concealed in the Seeds, arising naturally without art.

items.quote: planted in every growing thing by vertue of that omnipotent Word, whereby all things were brought out of darknesse into Light
items.note: The Creator planted this vertue in every growing thing at the Creation by the Word.

items.quote: The faculties and vertue therefore wherewith mixt bodies are indued (like the soule in mans body from the beginning of the Creation) is not from without
items.note: The vertue of mixt bodies is not from without; it is likened to the soul in man's body.

items.quote: nor infused into them by a momomentaneous position of the Stars, nor made up of a fortuitous meeting of Atomes
items.note: Two origins are denied: a position of the Stars, and a chance meeting of Atomes.

items.quote: it proceedeth not from the body nor the mixture of the body or visible forme, for then it could not be separated without the destruction and corruption of the body and forme
items.note: The vertue is not from the body or its mixture; the reason given is that it can be separated.

items.quote: as we see in Cinamon and Pepper, whose virtues being extracted either by art, or vanishing by age and long keeping
items.note: Example: the virtues of Cinamon and Pepper are extracted by art or vanish with keeping.

items.quote: the mecanick sciences of the Three principles
items.note: The Three principles are named as one thing; these lines do not say what they are.

items.quote: the actions of Cures proceed from the Spirits and vitall Tinctures of the spirits, not from the bodies or dead Relloceous qualities
items.note: Cures come from Spirits and vitall Tinctures, not from bodies or qualities. The word stands here as Relloceous, in CH2.2 as Relollaceous.

items.quote: Heaven is the framer of the externall edifices, not of the Secrets, Wonders and mysteries that dwell in them.
items.note: Margin note: Heaven frames the outward buildings, not the Secrets within them.

items.quote: it is granted by the Interpreters of Secret Nature, that there is nothing in the whole Universe, every particular whereof is not also in that Microcosm Man
items.name: the Interpreters of Secret Nature
items.note: The view that everything in the Universe is also in Man is given as granted by the Interpreters of Secret Nature.

items.quote: is not also in that Microcosm Man, as hath been said
items.note: Points back to an earlier place where this was said.

items.quote: the seeds of all things lye hid in him, as of the Stars, Meteors, Mineralls Vegetables, Animalls, Spirits, even of Daemoris, in respect of the Spirit of Man
items.note: The seeds of all things are said to lie hid in Man.

items.quote: this Symmetricall concord and Physicall anagoge
items.note: The likeness of Man and Universe is named a Symmetricall concord and Physicall anagoge.

items.quote: how they might borrow strengthning remedies from his Parent or the externall Heart of the Microcosm which is one like the other
items.note: True Physitians ask how remedies for the sick inner Heart may be borrowed from the outer Heart, the two being alike. The outer one is here printed as of the Microcosm.

items.quote: (if not in outward, yet in inward figure and forme)
items.note: The likeness of the two Hearts is said to be inward, not outward.

items.quote: which remedies are analogically represented
items.note: The remedies are said to be represented analogically.

items.quote: such as may many ways be got out of those three shops of Cures
items.note: The three Families are called three shops of Cures.

items.quote: For God created an inexhaustible supply of medicines, and distributed to every Country sufficient for it selfe.
items.note: God made medicines without end and gave each Country enough for itself.

items.quote: All the whole inferiour Nature is divided into three principall parts, i. e. Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall.
items.what: three principall parts, i. e. Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
items.note: Margin note states the division into three parts.

items.quote: Gold (which cheareth up the Spirits when a man hath enough of it in his purse)
items.note: Gold's cheering of the Spirits is turned to the purse: the words in brackets give a second, everyday sense.

items.quote: Antimony and the like, which are produced out of the Element of Water, as Gemms and precious stones in shells are generated of drops of water
items.note: Minerals such as Antimony are said to come from the Element of Water, like stones in shells from drops of water.

items.quote: which by a specifick and Harmonicall vertue serve to cure and comfort the heart
items.note: These things cure the heart by a specifick and Harmonicall vertue.

items.quote: Magicall and Hieroglyphicall Characters, which sage Antiquity hath without rashnesse or superstition attributed to them
items.note: Minerals are said to bear Magicall and Hieroglyphicall Characters, ascribed to them by Antiquity.

items.quote: Magically disclose their hidden vertue to those more secret Phylosophers that are instructed therein
items.note: The Characters disclose the hidden vertue only to instructed, more secret Phylosophers.

items.quote: by Natures just decree, with-hold their benigne and vitall Element from those that possesse them
items.note: The choicest things withhold their vitall Element from their possessors, by Nature's decree.

items.quote: many there are who confound the Universall Lawes of Nature, and yet thinks to partake of her Banquet in the end
items.note: Many confound Nature's laws and still expect her Banquet.

items.quote: if it were rightly refined, and had its power reduced into act by a Naturall and due Resolution, that it might exercise its vertues
items.note: Gold must be rightly refined and its power brought into act by a Resolution.

items.quote: (for there is but one way to Resolve and to compound things, because Art and Nature, like mother and daughter, consent to each other)
items.note: There is one way only to Resolve and compound; Art and Nature agree like mother and daughter.

items.quote: few men have this gift of God bestowed on them, so as to make solid and massy Gold potable, that it may be drunk
items.note: Making Gold potable is a gift of God that few men have.

items.quote: As he that hath much Gold may know nothing of its medicinall vertue.
items.note: Margin note: the owner of much Gold may not know its medicinal vertue.

items.quote: Art imitateth Nature and supplyeth its defects; it correcteth, chastiseth, assisteth and promoteth, yea it exceedeth Nature.
items.note: Margin note: Art imitates, mends and even exceeds Nature.

items.quote: Amongst Vegetables there is Saffron, Rue, Balme, Scordium, Celandine, Mace, Ocymum, with six hundred of the like.
items.note: The Vegetables are listed by name.

items.quote: Amongst Animalls there is
items.note: The Animalls are listed: horns and the Bone in Staggs hearts.

items.quote: All which being rightly prepared in due manner, doe cure the diseases of the Heart
items.note: The listed things cure diseases of the Heart once rightly prepared; the manner is not given in these lines.

items.quote: not (as I have said) by their Externall superficiary qualities
items.note: Points back to what the author has said before.

items.quote: but by an Internall, proper, specifick, harmonious, similer virtue
items.note: They cure by an inner, specifick, similer virtue, not by outward qualities.

items.quote: are all contained in the Spirits, which onely know how and where to find out the disease
items.note: What serves health is contained in the Spirits, which alone find the disease.

items.quote: the earthy part is altogether dead, husks and rinds beget nothing, the Spirits onely in the bodies of things doe all
items.note: The earthy part is dead; only the Spirits in bodies act.

items.quote: The Formes in thee medicines or Astra's of the medicaments separated by Alchymie from their bodies are the true Directoryes
items.note: The Formes or Astra's are separated from their bodies by Alchymie.

items.quote: not the body, but the Astrum or hidden Heaven gives all the direction
items.note: Astrum is glossed as hidden Heaven; it, not the body, directs.

items.quote: every medicine striveth to get to its place, and seeketh after that member that is like unto it
items.note: Each medicine seeks the member like itself.

items.quote: magnetick vertue which may well be called the inexpressible property
items.note: The magnetick vertue is given a name: the inexpressible property. A letter of the word before it could not be read.

items.quote: as the true Phylosophicall Phisitians have diligently observed by long Experience the most undouted Rule of all
items.name: the true Phylosophicall Phisitians
items.note: That like applies itself to like is given as observed by the true Phylosophicall Phisitians.

items.quote: Celsus the Roman Physitian confesseth of all Arts
items.name: Celsus
items.note: Celsus is named as confessing something of all Arts; the sentence as given does not say plainly what.

items.quote: where by many good old country women have gone beyond great learned Physitians
items.note: Country women are said to have gone beyond learned Physitians.

items.quote: The same may be sayd of the other six principall members and parts of mans body
items.what: the other six principall members and parts of mans body
items.note: Six further principall members are announced beside the Heart.

items.quote: The external Macrocosmicall Braine is the Oyle of Silver, Water of the Sophire Emerold, Mosse, Vitrioll
items.note: The outer Braine is said to be these named things, which strengthen the inner Braine of man.

items.quote: The flower or CHIBUR or Brimstone are a Balsam for the lungs and the whole breast.
items.note: CHIBUR stands beside flower and Brimstone, as a Balsam for lungs and breast.

items.quote: Experiment, as also judgement, without knowledge is but fallacious difficult and fortuitous, but with Science it is true and infallible.
items.note: Margin note: Experiment without knowledge is fallacious, with Science true.

items.quote: After this manner not only ordinary diseases are cured by every Dunce, but also those Chronicall, Astrall and fixed diseases which by many are accounted desperate
items.note: In this way long and Astrall diseases counted desperate are cured too.

items.quote: the common sort of Physitians who know not the seat, seeds, nativities, roots, and centres of diseases judge to be incurable
items.note: Common Physitians, not knowing the seat and seeds of diseases, judge them incurable.

items.quote: there is no disease, as it is a disease, but there is a medicine for it
items.note: Every disease has a medicine.

items.quote: unlesse such as prodeth onely from the anger of the Divine Majesty by secret predestination, which cannot be found out by man
items.note: The exception: disease from God's anger by secret predestination, which man cannot find out.

items.quote: the cure whereof was never given to Physitians, but to the Apostles, who by true faith in Christ healed all Diseases
items.note: The cure of such disease was given to the Apostles, not to Physitians.

items.quote: unlesse with Pliny we should belye Nature in its perfections as an unjust Step-mother
items.name: Pliny
items.note: The view of Nature as an unjust Step-mother is given to Pliny and rejected.

items.quote: whereas indeed she is the benigne Parent of all Things
items.note: The author's own view: Nature is the kind Parent of all things.

items.quote: provident and wise Nature hath by naturall instinct bestowed upon poor bruite creatures the knowledge of their Remedies
items.note: Nature gave beasts the knowledge of their remedies by instinct.

items.quote: It were therefore great folly and sottishnesse to think that the great Creator would hide these things from men
items.note: The author denies that the Creator would hide these things from men.

items.quote: to think that the great Creator would hide these things from men
items.note: Here hiding from men is denied; CH2.5 says the choicest things withhold their vitall Element and that few have the gift, and CH2.20 says the Word is not known to every one.

items.quote: There is no cause to complaine of the want of medicines but onely of our ignorance of them.
items.note: Margin note: not medicines are wanting, only knowledge of them.

items.quote: There are two sorts of Physitians, one cure miraculously, the other naturally by means.
items.note: Margin note sets out two sorts of Physitians.

items.quote: there are two originalls of every disease, the one naturall, the other caelestiall
items.note: Margin note sets out two originalls of every disease.

items.quote: the Caelestiall is cured by the Word of the Lord, the Naturall is recovered by naturall means
items.note: Margin note: each originall has its own cure.

items.quote: The Stork having eaten a Serpent, is cured with Organy.
items.note: First of a list of beasts each cured by a named herb.

items.quote: The Toad when stung or poysoned with any other venomous creature, eateth Rue, Sage or Plantin, or rubs the wounded part therewith and is recovered
items.note: The Toad heals itself with herbs, by eating or rubbing.

items.quote: therefore it is not good to eat Sage before it be washed
items.note: A plain piece of advice is drawn from the Toad's use of Sage.

items.quote: And other living creatures have found out other innumerable Hearbs.
items.note: The list closes: other creatures have found countless other herbs.

items.quote: Every Creature knoweth his proper remedy.
items.note: Margin note sums up the list.

items.quote: which he created after his own Image, and prefer the Beasts before them, for whose sake all things were created
items.note: It is denied that the Father would neglect his children, made after his Image, and prefer the Beasts.

items.quote: he that gave us his Son, and commanded us to pray for his Holy Spirit, how much rather will he subject the whole Creature, both things visible and invisible?
items.note: From the gift of the Son the author argues that the whole Creature will be subjected to men.

items.quote: created Medicines out of the Earth
items.name: Eccl. 38.
items.note: The margin note beside these words names Eccl. 38.

items.quote: not defectives but perfect, he hath commanded the Physitians to search them out and seasonably administer them to every distemper being by due faith prepared and made up
items.note: The Medicines are created perfect; Physitians are commanded to search them out and give them, prepared by faith.

items.quote: not defectives but perfect
items.note: Here Medicines out of the Earth are perfect; CH2.1 says whatever is in sublunary things has a perfect and an imperfect nature.

items.quote: become efficacious and obtaine their wholesome effect, not of it selfe, but by the gift of God
items.note: Medicines work by the gift of God, not of themselves.

items.quote: unlesse God be present and infuse virtue into the Hearbs what good can Dittany doe, or any other soveraigne medicine
items.note: Without God infusing virtue an herb does no good.

items.quote: All these inferiour things, as living creatures, hearbs, stones, mettalls have their force by subministration from the Heaven, and the Heaven from the Intelligences, and these from the great Worker
items.note: A chain of force: lower things from the Heaven, the Heaven from the Intelligences, these from the great Worker.

items.quote: have their force by subministration from the Heaven
items.note: Here lower things have their force from the Heaven; CH2.3 says the vertue is not from without nor infused by a position of the Stars, and N133 that Heaven does not frame the Secrets.

items.quote: the Elements live by the Firmament, the Firmament from the Intelligible World, and this onely in God, or his Eternall Word
items.note: The same chain for life: Elements, Firmament, Intelligible World, God or his Word.

items.quote: the onely life of all, and in all, yet variously sprouting forth according to the subject into which it flows
items.note: God is the one life in all, showing differently by the subject it flows into.

items.quote: if we intend to doe any good with hearbs, we must not trust so much to them as to God
items.note: Trust is to be placed in God more than in herbs.

items.quote: Asa dyed because he trusted more to the Physitians then to God.
items.name: 2 Chro. 16.12.
items.note: The margin note beside these words names 2 Chro. 16.12.

items.quote: Will of the Lord is earnestly to be implored
items.note: Margin note: not Nature but the Will of the Lord is to be implored.

items.quote: The Caelestiall Medicine onely, or the WORD of God (which is the Firmament of all Physick
items.note: The Caelestiall Medicine is equated with the WORD of God, and called the Firmament of all Physick.

items.quote: without which no drug will doe good) is that which healeth all things
items.name: Psal. 33. & 107.20. Eccl. 38.9, 10, 11, 12.
items.note: The margin note beside these words names Psal. 33. & 107.20. and Eccl. 38.9, 10, 11, 12.

items.quote: by the efficacy of the WORD (in which lyeth hid, and from which proceedeth all force beyond any naturall actions) all Medicines become powerfull
items.note: All force is said to lie hid in the WORD; by it Medicines have power.

items.quote: As the bark is not the kernell, so hearbs are not the medicines, but a signe onely of the Word signified.
items.note: Herbs are said not to be the medicines but only a signe of the Word.

items.quote: Physick is two-fold in the Earth
items.note: Physick is set out as two: Visible and Invisible.

items.quote: ought not to be administred before there be a separation of the pure from the impure
items.note: Visible Physick is to be given only after the pure is separated from the impure.

items.quote: Invisible, from the Son by the Word, and is but one
items.note: Invisible Physick is from the Son by the Word, and is one only.

items.quote: the Hearb is not the medicine, for that is invisibly hid in God himselfe
items.note: The medicine is said to be hid invisibly in God himself.

items.quote: for that is invisibly hid in God himselfe
items.note: Here the medicine is hid in God himself; CH2.2 says the specifix vertue is concealed in the very Seeds, and this paragraph itself speaks of the Hearbs in which the medicine is.

items.quote: we shall not wonder that Almighty God could (and can) make men whole by the Prophets and True Cabalists with a word onely
items.note: God heals through Prophets and True Cabalists with a word only. The margin note at the end of the sentence names Acts 3.6.

items.quote: God is a living God, the NAME also of the living God is lively, and so the Letters of the living Name are also lively
items.note: Life passes from God to his NAME and from the Name to its Letters.

items.quote: as God hath life in himselfe, so hath he given to his Name to have life in it selfe, and the Name also to the Letters
items.note: The same chain restated as a gift of life.

items.quote: True Magicians (by whom I doe not mean Nicromancers or them of the Black Art) those accurate searchers out of Nature
items.note: The author says whom he means by True Magicians: searchers out of Nature, not Nicromancers.

items.quote: framed at a certaine time according to the power of Heaven
items.note: The Word written and the Characters or Signes are framed at a certain time by the power of Heaven.

items.quote: far from all superstition, which ariseth onely from ignorance, without any prophanation or scandall of the Divine Majesty, or any wrong to Faith and Religion
items.note: The author holds this free of superstition and of wrong to religion.

items.quote: otherwise it were better for us alwayes to be sick then to be cured with the dishonour of God
items.note: Better sick than cured with dishonour of God.

items.quote: Characters or constellated Names according to Agrippa, have no force from the Figureors Pronunciation, but by reason of the Vertue or Office which God or Nature hath ordained to such a Name or Character
items.name: Agrippa
items.note: The view that Characters have force from an ordained Vertue or Office, not from figure or pronunciation, is given to Agrippa.

items.quote: There is no vertue or power either in Heaven or Earth which descendeth not from God, nor can it give or actually exercise any thing it hath but by his permission.
items.note: All vertue descends from God and acts by his permission.

items.quote: Such Names are the Divine Power.
items.note: Margin note: such Names are the Divine Power.

items.quote: Medicines are visible bodies; Words are invisible bodies
items.note: Medicines and Words are both called bodies, visible and invisible.

items.quote: by the Spirit of God made One with Nature by his Word FIAT
items.note: Herb or Word heals by the Spirit of God made one with Nature by the Word FIAT.

items.quote: Concerning Characteristicalll Cure which affecteth Naturall operations by words pronounced, written, carved and hanged about the neck
items.note: A kind of cure is named: by words spoken, written, carved, hung about the neck.

items.quote: let him read Rog. Bacon of the wonderfull power of Art and Nature
items.name: Rog. Bacon
items.note: The reader is sent to Rog. Bacon for this kind of cure.

items.quote: Paracels. saith that Characters are
items.name: Paracels.
items.note: Margin note gives Paracels. a saying on Characters; letters of it could not be read.

items.quote: Physitians also have wrought great cures by the Created Word, or the incarnate Mercy
items.note: Created Word is put beside incarnate Mercy; the same paragraph later says increated Mercy.

items.quote: all these things are done by the efficacy of the Triune and Divine Word onely, which healeth and preserveth all things
items.note: All cures are done by the Divine Word only.

items.quote: as we see in our Saviour miracles, who when he restored the deafe and dumb
items.name: Luke 11.14.
items.note: The margin note beside these words names Luke 11.14.

items.quote: he did it by One Word, and he is that Word, to wit, the increated Mercy of God
items.note: The Saviour is said to be the Word, the increated Mercy of God.

items.quote: by which are all created things, from which all simples flow, which also with the Father dayly worketh all in all
items.name: John 1.3. Mat. 4.4.
items.note: The margin note beside these words names John 1.3. and Mat. 4.4.

items.quote: all that for certaine is wrought of God incarnate in his explicit and manifest bond of one Spirit filling all things inseperably gathered into one
items.note: All vertue in creatures, in great and little world, is wrought by God incarnate in one Spirit that fills all.

items.quote: which Spirit therefore is the only fulnes of the whole world
items.note: This Spirit is named the fulnes of the world, called The Fulnesse; the margin note beside it names Eccl. 24.8, 9, 10, 11.

items.quote: Nothing is made out of God, for in him all things live, are moved and doe subsist.
items.note: Nothing is made outside God.

items.quote: Grace exceedeth Nature, and the thing signified excelleth the signe.
items.note: Margin note: Grace above Nature, the thing signified above the signe.

items.quote: This WORD of God, the First begotten of every Creature, is truly our Dayly Bread for which our Saviour commanded us to pray
items.note: The WORD is said to be the Dayly Bread.

items.quote: it is the supercaelestiall Mummy, the supernaturall Balsome comforting poor Mortalls more then Mans own Mummy or naturall Balsom
items.note: The WORD is called supercaelestiall Mummy and supernaturall Balsome, set above man's own Mummy or naturall Balsom.

items.quote: The vertue in bread is the blessing of God, yea God himselfe: the Word in our Earthly food is the true Bread which is given to good and bad
items.note: The vertue in bread is God's blessing; the Word in food is the true Bread.

items.quote: Man liveth not by bread alone, but by that which is in Bread
items.note: Man lives by what is in bread.

items.quote: If the Word were not, or of it selfe were not the onely Bread, then the Earth would be our God, but that may not be
items.note: Argument: were the Word not the only Bread, the Earth would be our God.

items.quote: Without this benediction the staffe of bread is broken
items.note: Margin note: without the blessing the staffe of bread is broken.

items.quote: It is of mere mercy and goodnesse not of justice that we have both the bread of nourishment and of healing.
items.note: Margin note: bread of nourishment and of healing come of mercy, not justice.

items.quote: This Word then is the true medicine that healeth all things, but is not known to every one
items.note: The Word, the true medicine, is not known to every one; the lines add that not every Scholler can write of it.

items.quote: our friend Theophrastus Paracelsus a Disciple of the Mosaicall and Living Phylosophy hath written of the Secrets of Nature and the Wonders of God
items.name: Theophrastus Paracelsus
items.note: Theophrastus Paracelsus is named as having written of this.

items.quote: to wit, of the WORD of God INCARNATE which may be found in the Creatures
items.note: The Secrets and Wonders are glossed as the WORD of God INCARNATE, to be found in the Creatures.

items.quote: by this Word, FIAT, the seed of the whole world, were Heaven and Earth created, and this is that which is efficacious in all the Creatures
items.note: FIAT is called the seed of the whole world and that which works in all Creatures. The margin note beside the paragraph names John 1.10. Heb. 11.3. Psal. 107.20.

items.quote: to which the Creatures are justly in subjection as to their own soule
items.note: Creatures are subject to this Word as to their own soul.

items.quote: that the MAGUS, the Wise man or Caelestiall Physitian performeth suddenly and much sooner by Characters and Stones with a most powerfull impression
items.note: MAGUS is glossed as the Wise man or Caelestiall Physitian; he does at once by Characters and Stones what the Physitian does in time by HEARBS.

items.quote: to wit, the Gamahaea of Influentiall Wedlock to the Terrestiall signe, by matrimoniall combination of the Superiors and Inferiors ASTRALLY
items.note: The impression is glossed as the Gamahaea, a wedlock of Superiors and Inferiors.

items.quote: like a stretched cord, all the Superiour vertue floweth through every inferiour thing even to the utmost
items.note: The tie of Nature is put as a likeness: a stretched cord.

items.quote: the inferiour passe through all to their Superiours, because the working Vertue is one, and the participation of the species is diffused through all
items.note: Lower things pass up to higher, because the working Vertue is one.

items.quote: Divine Matrimony; Hence is that wonderfull tye, continuity, influence and simpathy between inferiour & superiour Naturall things
items.note: The tie of higher and lower is named Divine Matrimony.

items.quote: many things may be done in Magick and Cabal by the intercession of the worlds marriage
items.note: Much may be done in Magick and Cabal through the world's marriage.

items.quote: The explication of a common saving (1) in Hearbs Stones and Words there are great vertues.
items.what: in Hearbs Stones and Words there are great vertues
items.note: Margin note calls the passage the explication of a common saying about Hearbs, Stones and Words.

items.quote: the True Cabalist (whom Paracelsus calls the Naturall Divine, who is equall to the Prophets
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: The name Naturall Divine for the True Cabalist is given to Paracelsus.

items.quote: whose mind being united and coaequant to God doth whatsoever he will, for he willeth onely what God doth
items.note: The Cabalist's mind is united to God and wills only what God does.

items.quote: he doth above Nature, DEALLY or like God accomplish complish in a moment by firme confidence and strong faith
items.note: DEALLY is glossed as like God; the work is done above Nature, in a moment, by faith.

items.quote: the very GATE of miracles in that Only Divine Name ISHUH in which all things are reckoned up and contained
items.note: A Name is set apart: ISHUH, in which all things are contained.

items.quote: he doth performe it in the WONDERFULL WORD by the Mind, Faith and Prayer, to wit, prayers made in Spirit and in Truth
items.note: Doing it in the Name is glossed: in the WONDERFULL WORD, by Mind, Faith and Prayer.

items.quote: The New Birth is the Field of Caelestiall Physick which healeth with a word without Externall means
items.note: The New Birth is called the Field of Caelestiall Physick.

items.quote: that one operation is in respect of God as the Artificer, and in respect of Man as the Instrument
items.note: In this work God is the Artificer, Man the Instrument.

items.quote: every creature is at the beck and command of their faith who are men innocent and taught in the Law of the Lord
items.note: Every creature obeys the faith of innocent men taught in the Law of the Lord.

items.quote: who are heard in all things whatsoever they pray for, witnesse Elias, Elisha
items.name: Elias, Elisha
items.note: Elias and Elisha are called as witnesses; the margin note names the books of the Kings, 1 Kings 3.12. and Wifd. 7.

items.quote: I mean (not a lazy, sluggish prayer, but) a constant asking, seeking, knocking
items.note: The author says what he means by prayer.

items.quote: by faithfull Prayer we ascend in a straite and most sure way to the highest Wisdome of Divine and humane Things
items.note: Faithful Prayer is the sure way to the highest Wisdome.

items.quote: in these Three principall Poynts also consisteth the whole Foundation of the Magicall and Cabalisticall Art, as appeareth by Paracelsus in his third book of the Signature of Things
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: The Three principall Poynts as the foundation of the Magicall and Cabalisticall Art are referred to a named book of Paracelsus.

items.quote: Every Creature feareth and reverenceth his Name that made it.
items.note: Margin note: every creature reveres its maker's Name.

items.quote: Honour and Praise and Glory therefore belongeth to the Creator, who worketh all in all, for the desired successe of his Medicine or Word which he hath given
items.note: The praise for a cure belongs to the Creator.

items.quote: the Physitian who is the obedient Minister of God and Nature
items.note: The Physitian is called Minister of God and Nature.

items.quote: there is no other reward due but that of his faithfull paines and Charity
items.note: The Physitian is due only the reward of his pains and Charity.

items.quote: there is nothing at all of his own in it besides Art and right preparation
items.note: Only Art and right preparation are the Physitian's own.

items.quote: God who alone is to be praised and blessed in all, and over all, will not give his Honour to another
items.note: God keeps his Honour to himself.

items.quote: We are not to ascribe our bodily health to the Physitian but to God.
items.note: Margin note: health is to be ascribed to God.

items.quote: proudly and rashly promise a set and certaine time of recovery which is to be left to God onely
items.note: Margin note rebukes Physitians who promise a set time of recovery.

items.quote: is to be honoured as the Scripture commandeth
items.name: the Scripture
items.note: The honour due to the true Physitian is given as the Scripture's command. The paragraph opens with Neverthelesse, after CH2.23.

items.quote: the true and sincere Physitian, who among all arts and faculties is most accepted of God
items.note: The true Physitian is most accepted of God among all arts.

items.quote: First, because God worketh and doth his own will by him as by his Minister, when he sleepeth and knoweth it not
items.note: First of three numbered reasons for honouring the Physitian.

items.quote: by affording Physick enough from the Earth, and his Word from above, without which nothing can be efficacious to our health
items.note: God gives Physick from the Earth and his Word from above; without the Word nothing works.

items.quote: saith our Saviour, ye can nothing
items.name: our Saviour
items.note: Words given to our Saviour; the margin note names John 15.

items.quote: Secondly, because (Health being the greatest Good to men) he ought to excell all mortalls in the search and knowledge of Nature and the Light thereof
items.note: Second reason: the Physitian ought to excel in the knowledge of Nature and its Light.

items.quote: Not in vaine therefore did Homer require a Physitian to be furnished with all knowledge in respect of those small cures which he is to doe.
items.name: Homer
items.note: Homer is named as requiring all knowledge of a Physitian; a margin note in foreign script stands beside it.

items.quote: Thirdly, because he alone manifesteth to all, the wonderfull works of God both in the great and little world
items.note: Third reason: the Physitian shows the works of God in the great and little world.

items.quote: not onely by opening his mysteryes and hidden secrets, but also by curing the sick
items.note: The Physitian is said to open God's mysteries and hidden secrets.

items.quote: among all Sciences and Faculties, Physick is to be accounted the most excellent, wherein the greatest wonders of God are miraculously seen
items.note: Physick is the most excellent of the Sciences.

items.quote: It taketh its rise from Theology or the Light of Grace, and endeth in the Light of Nature.
items.note: Theology is equated with the Light of Grace; Physick begins there and ends in the Light of Nature.
